verdict.summary: You can create a HubSpot OAuth app and install it in your own account in minutes, with no review. Review applies only to a Marketplace listing. A listing needs 3 active installs on accounts outside your organization, and HubSpot does an initial manual review within 10 business days. Certification is optional and much harder (6 months listed, 60 installs). The sources don't clearly confirm whether an unlisted app can be installed by any HubSpot account.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for your own app; 1-2 days to prepare a Marketplace listing
verdict.approval_wait: None to install in your own account. If you list on the Marketplace, the initial review takes up to 10 business days, and the full feedback cycle can take up to 60 days.

gates.name: Your own app, installed in your own account
gates.unlocks: You can connect your own HubSpot account through your own client ID and secret in Composio.
limits: The person installing must be a Super Admin or have HubSpot Marketplace Access permission
Scopes marked Enterprise-only work only on Enterprise accounts
A redirect URI on http://localhost is allowed for testing; production needs https and a domain name, not an IP

gates.name: Unlisted installs on other HubSpot accounts
gates.unlocks: Customer or test accounts can install the app from your install (authorize) URL without a Marketplace listing.
limits: Whether any account can install an unlisted app, or only allowlisted accounts, is not confirmed (see open questions)
OAuth apps are limited to 110 requests per 10 seconds per installing account
Each installer must be a Super Admin or have Marketplace Access permission
You need 3 active, unaffiliated production installs from this stage before you can list on the Marketplace

gates.name: HubSpot App Marketplace listing (certification optional)
gates.unlocks: Users can find the app on the HubSpot Marketplace. Certification adds a certified badge later.
limits: You can submit only one app for approval at a time
OAuth must be the only auth method, with least-privilege scopes
Certification: listed at least 6 months, at least 60 unaffiliated installs, verified domain, demo video, security questionnaire, success rate of 95% or higher; certified status lasts 2 years
Listing and certification are free, with no revenue share
gates.time_to_reach: Several weeks or more: get 3 unaffiliated installs, then about 10 business days for initial review and up to 60 days of feedback. Certification needs another 6+ months.

steps.title: Sign in or create a HubSpot developer account
steps.detail: Go to developers.hubspot.com and create a developer account, or sign in. Since the September 2025 platform launch, developer and CRM accounts are combined, so an existing CRM account may already show a Development tab where you can create and install apps.
gotchas: The app must be linked to a developer-enabled account.

steps.title: Create a new app
steps.detail: In the developer platform (Development tab), create a new app. Enter the app name, description, logo and support info. Users see these on the authorization screen.
gotchas: If you plan to list it, the app must cover its own use case. HubSpot asks you to merge similar apps that use the same APIs.

steps.title: Set the redirect URI on the Auth page
steps.detail: In the app settings, open the Auth page and add the Composio callback URL as the redirect URI.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Production redirect URIs must use https and a domain name, not an IP address. http://localhost is allowed only for testing.

steps.title: Choose a minimal scope set
steps.detail: Compare the tools your agent needs with HubSpot's scope reference. Mark only the scopes you truly need as required, and mark the rest as optional or conditionally required. Do not copy Composio's full default list: several names in it (e.g. accounting, tickets, timeline, e-commerce, content) could not be matched to HubSpot's scope reference. HubSpot adds the oauth scope to every app automatically.
gotchas: The scope parameter in Composio's auth config must include every required scope, or the authorization page shows an error.
Sensitive and highly sensitive CRM scopes are Enterprise-only, so they will fail on lower-tier accounts.

steps.title: Copy the client credentials into Composio
steps.detail: On the app's Auth page, copy the Client ID and Client Secret. Paste them into a new HubSpot auth config in Composio, with the same scopes you set in HubSpot.
gotchas: HubSpot uses a confidential client with a client secret. According to one source, PKCE is not supported.

steps.title: Test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio and approve it while signed in as a Super Admin or a user with Marketplace Access permission. Check that the code is exchanged for tokens and that tokens refresh based on expires_in.
gotchas: HubSpot's official page shows /oauth/v3/token, but Composio's toolkit uses api.hubapi.com/oauth/v1/token. Check which one works before you hardcode either.
Refresh tokens on a schedule. HubSpot says a 401 response is not a valid signal to fetch a new token.

steps.title: Install the app on customer or test accounts
steps.detail: Share the install URL with other HubSpot accounts and have an admin in each account approve it. If you add scopes later, existing users must re-authorize through a new install URL that includes the added scopes.
gotchas: The sources don't confirm whether unlisted apps can be installed by any account or only by allowlisted accounts.

steps.title: Prepare listing materials
steps.detail: Draft and publish a privacy policy, terms of service, a support contact, and public setup documentation. The documentation must not sit behind a login or paywall and must include screenshots of the scope approval screen.
gotchas: The URLs must be live and publicly reachable.

steps.title: Reach three unaffiliated production installs
steps.detail: Before you submit the listing, get at least 3 active, unique production installs in the past 30 days from accounts unaffiliated with your organization.
gotchas: Test accounts and accounts affiliated with your organization don't count.

steps.title: Submit the Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Submit the listing from the developer platform. Make sure OAuth is the only auth method, the scopes are least privilege, and the app doesn't use classic CRM cards.
gotchas: You can submit only one app at a time. Any other app submitted while one is in review is rejected automatically.

steps.title: Wait for Ecosystem Quality review
steps.detail: HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team reviews the listing manually. The initial review finishes within 10 business days. After feedback is shared, the full process should take no more than 60 days.

steps.title: (Optional) Apply for certification later
steps.detail: After the app has been listed for at least 6 months and has 60 or more unaffiliated installs, you can apply for certification. You need a verified domain, a demo video, a security questionnaire about how you access and store OAuth tokens, a success rate of 95% or higher, and 429 errors under 5% of daily requests.
gotchas: HubSpot won't review without the demo video. Certified status lasts 2 years, then must be renewed.

requirements.detail: The app must be linked to a developer account. CRM accounts now include a Development tab.

requirements.item: Installer is a Super Admin or has Marketplace Access permission
requirements.detail: This applies to every account that installs the app.

requirements.item: https redirect URI on a domain
requirements.detail: http://localhost is allowed only while testing.

requirements.item: Required scopes match the scope parameter
requirements.detail: Otherwise the authorization page shows an error.

requirements.item: 3 unaffiliated active production installs in the past 30 days
requirements.detail: Needed before you can submit the Marketplace listing.

requirements.item: Public privacy policy, terms, support contact and setup docs
requirements.detail: The setup docs must not be behind a login and must include screenshots of the scope approval screen.

requirements.item: Least-privilege scopes, with OAuth as the only auth method
requirements.detail: Remove any scopes you don't use.
Verified domain, demo video, security questionnaire, 6 months listed, 60 installs, success rate of 95% or higher.

scopes.effect: HubSpot adds this scope to every app automatically.

scopes.scope: Sensitive / highly sensitive contact, company, deal and custom-object scopes
scopes.effect: Enterprise-only, so installs on lower-tier accounts will fail if these are required. Make them optional instead.

scopes.scope: accounting, tickets, timeline, e-commerce, content (from Composio's default list)
scopes.effect: Could not be matched to HubSpot's scope reference. Check them, or remove them before installing or submitting for review.

blockers.symptom: The authorization page shows a scope error
blockers.cause: A scope marked required in Auth settings is missing from the requested scope parameter
blockers.fix: Make the scopes in Composio's auth config match the required scopes exactly, and move extra scopes to optional_scope.

blockers.symptom: A user cannot install the app
blockers.cause: The user is not a Super Admin and lacks Marketplace Access permission, or the app requests Enterprise-only scopes on a lower-tier account
blockers.fix: Have an admin install it, and make tier-restricted scopes optional or conditionally required.

blockers.symptom: A second app submission is rejected automatically
blockers.cause: Only one app can be in review at a time
blockers.fix: Wait until the first review finishes, then submit the next app.

blockers.symptom: The listing is rejected for UI extensions
blockers.cause: Classic CRM cards are not supported as of June 16, 2025
blockers.fix: Move to the current UI extension model before you submit.

blockers.symptom: The listing or certification review flags unused scopes
blockers.cause: Every requested scope must be used
blockers.fix: Remove the extra scopes. Existing users then re-authorize through a new install URL if scopes change.

blockers.cause: The token endpoint path differs between sources (v1 vs v3)
blockers.fix: Test both /oauth/v1/token and /oauth/v3/token, then use the one that works.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed HubSpot OAuth to test quickly. Register your own public app when you want your own branding on the consent screen, your own redirect, your own rate-limit budget, or a Marketplace listing. Creating your own app takes about 30 minutes with no review. Trim Composio's long default scope list to what your app actually uses before installing it on customer accounts or submitting for review.

evidence.claim: Composio lists managed OAuth for HubSpot with OAUTH2 mode and HubSpot authorize and token URLs.
Composio's guide says to create a developer account and a public app, then copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the Auth tab into Composio.
A developer account is needed because the public app must be linked to one.
The HubSpot developer portal landing page loads without a login wall and offers creating a developer account.
You create a new app in the developer platform; the client ID and secret are on the app's Auth page.
Since September 2025, developer and CRM accounts are combined; CRM accounts show a Development tab for creating apps.
App name, description, logo and support info are shown to users at authentication.
Any app meant for several HubSpot accounts or for the Marketplace must use OAuth.
Installing users must be a Super Admin or hold Marketplace Access permission.
The redirect URI is set on the Auth settings page; it must use https in production (localhost http allowed for testing) and a domain, not an IP.
Required scopes must appear in the scope parameter or the authorization page shows an error; optional scopes go in optional_scope.
The code is exchanged at the OAuth v3 token endpoint, and the access token is refreshed with the refresh token.
Composio and a third-party tutorial give the token endpoint as api.hubapi.com/oauth/v1/token, which differs from the official v3 path.
HubSpot does not support PKCE for its OAuth flow; it uses a confidential client with a client secret.
Apps must refresh tokens on their own schedule using expires_in; a 401 is not a valid refresh signal.
Scopes are declared as required, conditionally required, or optional; OAuth apps can use the latter two.
Sensitive and highly sensitive CRM scopes are Enterprise-only; the oauth scope is added to all apps by default.
crm.objects.contacts.read and crm.objects.contacts.write are available to all accounts.
Certification requires every requested scope to be used; extraneous scopes must be removed.
Listing requires at least three active, unique, unaffiliated production installs in the past 30 days, OAuth as the sole auth method, and least-privilege scopes.
Listing submissions are manually reviewed; the initial review takes up to 10 business days and the full process up to 60 days from feedback.
Only one app can be submitted for approval at a time; others are rejected automatically.
Certification needs a demo video, a security questionnaire and a public security assessment; there is no review without the video.
Certification requires the app to be associated with a verified domain.
Certification requires six months listed and 60 active unaffiliated installs; test accounts don't count.
Certification has a 95% success-rate threshold and expects 429s under 5% of daily requests.
Listing requires public privacy policy and terms URLs, a support contact, and public setup docs with scope approval screenshots.
Listing and certification are free with no revenue share; certification lasts two years.
Classic CRM cards are not supported as of June 16, 2025, so apps using them cannot be listed.
Each app must address a separate use case; similar apps should be consolidated.
Marketplace OAuth apps are limited to 110 requests per 10 seconds per installing account.
Marketplace OAuth apps must use stable public API versions and keep a success rate above 95%.
Scopes can be added after install, but existing users must re-authorize through a new install URL.
The HubSpot OAuth authorize endpoint is reachable and returned a live page for an invalid client_id.
Because listing requires 3 unaffiliated production installs before submission, an unlisted, unreviewed app can presumably be installed by outside accounts.

open_questions: Can any HubSpot account install an unlisted, unreviewed app, or only allowlisted accounts? Official docs mention allowlisted distribution, but this was not confirmed.
Which token endpoint is correct: /oauth/v3/token (official page) or api.hubapi.com/oauth/v1/token (Composio)? Check before you hardcode either.
Refresh token lifetime and expiry behavior were not found on official pages.
Several Composio default scopes (accounting, tickets, timeline, e-commerce, content) could not be checked against HubSpot's current scope reference.
The OAuth quickstart page returned 404, so the step-by-step console labels are not verified beyond the Auth page.
Rate-limit figures differ: 110 vs 100 requests per 10 seconds for OAuth apps. HubSpot's official usage page says 110.
How the authorize endpoint rejects unknown client IDs is not known from the probe.
